coverage: Inspected native circuit symbols, exported connectivity, full ERC/DRC records and saved-board pad assignments. Compared 694 numbered pads against the schematic netlist: no net-name mismatches.
Checked CAN transceiver pin identities and nominal supplies, MAX9924 default mode, MAX9142 comparator pin compatibility, added lowside interfaces and TLE9201 input defaults.
Confirmed R36/R37 are both 120 ohm, DNP and excluded from the BOM in the native schematic and saved board.
Verified the disposable VR sheet alias is byte-identical to the lowercase source; saved-board hash matches the packet.

Performed an analytical and ngspice resistor-only DC check of undriven LS9/LS10 bias. Commands, references, assumptions and limitations are recorded in review-work/circuit/experiments/review_log.md and driver_analysis.md.

findings.condition: Added lowside outputs commanded high through the documented Polygonus 3.3 V MCU interface.

U11–U14 and U16–U19 SOT-223 footprints, pad 1 connections

Section 1: drive-voltage bound and operating-range calculation

findings.location: Both Lowside Adder instances: U11–U14/U16–U19 and RN2/RN4
findings.mechanism: The SOT-223 N3 devices internally connect INPUT to their control supply. Their specified operating minimum is 3.5 V, while these channels receive at most nominal 3.3 V through series resistors.
findings.reasoning: Even ideal GPIO drive has 3.3−3.5 = −0.2 V operating-range margin before output and resistor drops. Both the named [VNL5090N3](https://www.st.com/resource/en/datasheet/vnl5090n3-e.pdf) and purchasing-selected [VNL5050N3](https://www.st.com/resource/en/datasheet/vnl5050n3-e.pdf) have this limitation. Turn-on and specified on-resistance are therefore unsupported by the interface. Actual loaded switching was not measured.
findings.title: Added lowside drivers receive less than their minimum operating drive

findings.condition: +5V is present while J2.24 and J2.25 are undriven, such as before MCU output initialization.

evidence.locator: R2 at line 20109 and R1 at line 20669, both 1k pullups
RN1 1k pulldowns, RN2 1k series branches, U11/U12 INPUT pins
Explicit ideal-resistor model and unloaded-input assumptions
Operating-point results: control and driver both 2.500000 V

findings.mechanism: Each populated 1k pullup opposes a 1k pulldown, producing a nominal unloaded 2.5 V input bias instead of a defined low state.
findings.reasoning: The passive calculation and restricted simulation agree: 5×1k/(1k+1k)=2.5 V, with 1.5k Thevenin resistance at the driver input. This lies within the N3 devices’ specified 1–3.5 V threshold interval, so unwanted conduction cannot be excluded. Driver loading, initialization timing and actuator response remain unmeasured; an actual startup actuation is not established.
findings.title: Undriven LS9/LS10 have an uncertain switch state

findings.condition: Driver identity is obtained from the saved value and purchasing fields.

SKU C2680415 maps to MPN VNL5050N3TR-E

findings.location: U11–U14 and U16–U19 component identity fields
findings.mechanism: The value identifies VNL5090, while the purchasing code selects VNL5050N3TR-E.
findings.reasoning: The [supplier’s C2680415 record](https://www.lcsc.com/product-detail/C2680415.html) identifies a different device from the schematic value. These devices have different published resistance and protection characteristics, leaving the intended fitted identity ambiguous. No harmful substitution outcome is asserted.
findings.title: Lowside driver values conflict with their purchasing code

limitations: Actual ECU module revision, fitted parts and firmware were not supplied. Retrieved upstream module sources are pinned references, not proof of the assembled module.

Internal CAN2 end-to-end termination and communication remain unverified: both base terminators are DNP; a reference Polygonus implementation contains one 120-ohm terminator. No mandatory short-bus topology, harness termination or waveform measurements were supplied, so no deterministic CAN failure is alleged.

No validated active-device simulation or hardware measurements covered startup, shutdown, brownout, VR response, ignition switching or actuator behavior. The added simulation proves passive DC bias only.
Omitted full rail-current budgets, automotive transients, ignition energy, wideband stability, EMC, thermal qualification, Atlas internals and integrated FOME-MC coverage.

Physical manufacturing/layout adjudication and individual disposition of every native warning were omitted. Saved copper was not refilled or modified; successful check exits and matching net names do not establish electrical behavior.
